title: Record which attack each of A, B, C, D produces for Earthquake and Nakoruru
description: Decision on 21 Sep 2026: do not assume the button-to-attack mapping. In a live Earthquake vs Nakoruru match started by lua/start_match.lua, use the Lua input helpers to press each of P1 A, P1 B, P1 C, P1 D for Earthquake and P2 A, P2 B, P2 C, P2 D for Nakoruru, standing, one at a time with a pause between, while I watch. Record for each button what came out (e.g. light slash, medium slash, heavy slash, kick, or whatever is seen) and which one is the character's heavy normal, as a data table in lua/moves_earthquake.lua and lua/moves_nakoruru.lua, and in notes. Log the frame of each press to /tmp/sam2/buttons.txt. This table is what intent "attack" maps to in the executor.
acceptance_criteria: 1) lua/moves_earthquake.lua and lua/moves_nakoruru.lua each contain a table with an observed attack for A, B, C and D and one entry marked heavy. 2) I confirm on screen what each button produced for each character, and that the entry marked heavy matches what I saw. 3) /tmp/sam2/buttons.txt lists the eight presses with frame numbers.

title: Run a full Earthquake vs Nakoruru match, Jev vs Jev, with no human input, and watch it
description: Owns PRD section 12 item: "Character contrast holds in play". Start the Stage 2 stack via /start-app with MAME windowed so we can both watch, and let a complete match run (until the game declares a winner) with no human input. Keep /tmp/sam2/bridge.log and /tmp/sam2/presses.log. While watching, note whether Earthquake plays as large, slow and long-reaching and Nakoruru as small, fast and mobile (PRD section 2), or whether the same questions produce indistinguishable play. This task does not tune anything (PRD section 4, out of scope); it records what was seen.
acceptance_criteria: 1) I confirm on screen that a full match ran to a declared winner with no human input. 2) /tmp/sam2/bridge.log covers the whole match with no gap longer than 2 seconds between calls for either fighter. 3) Notes state the section 12 verification result for character contrast in one or two sentences of what I saw.

title: Executor: intent to frame-accurate button sequences, facing-aware, with press source tagged
description: Decision on 21 Sep 2026: the executor lives in the Lua script; the bridge sends intent only. Replace the minimal expansion from the action-reader task with a proper executor: action.json carries per fighter an intent, a seq and a source; the executor expands it over the following frames. advance / retreat walk toward / away from the opponent using both X positions from the memory map, so it is facing-aware on either side; block holds away; attack performs the character's heavy normal exactly as recorded in the A/B/C/D observation task (never assumed); bait performs a normal at range then steps back. Normals and movement only; no special moves in v1 (PRD section 4). Each generated press is logged with frame, fighter, buttons and source (jev / reflex / start-sequence) to /tmp/sam2/presses.log; the bridge reads press counts per source from a field in state.json. Per-character tables live in lua/moves_earthquake.lua and lua/moves_nakoruru.lua.
acceptance_criteria: 1) I confirm on screen that each of the five intents, injected one at a time by a test action.json, produces the described behaviour for P1 Earthquake and for P2 Nakoruru, including correct direction after the fighters cross sides. 2) I confirm that intent attack produces the heavy normal recorded for that character. 3) /tmp/sam2/presses.log shows presses with frame numbers and a source field.

title: Replace the dummy with Jev in the bridge: 3 Hz per fighter, parallel, newest wins
description: Wire bridge/jev.py in as the DecisionMaker. Per fighter, a call is issued every 333 ms on its own worker; both fighters run in parallel. Each response carries the seq of the state it was asked about; a response is applied only if it is newer than the last applied one for that fighter, otherwise it is counted as stale and dropped (PRD section 8 item 5). The game loop must never wait on a call. The bridge writes the chosen intent to action.json; Lua expands it. Log per call: fighter, seq sent, seq of last applied, round-trip ms, intent, applied or stale, input and output tokens, to /tmp/sam2/bridge.log. Run a live match using the minimal Lua expansion from the action-reader task.
acceptance_criteria: 1) I confirm on screen a live Earthquake vs Nakoruru match in which both characters act on Jev decisions with no human input for at least 60 seconds. 2) /tmp/sam2/bridge.log shows about 3 calls per second per fighter, each with round-trip ms, intent, tokens, and an applied or stale mark. 3) Notes quote the p50 round trip from the log.

title: Jev client: build request from state, parse response, unit-tested against the saved sample
description: bridge/jev.py: build the PRD section 9 request for one fighter from a state.json object and the derived last-three-opponent-actions: model jev-latest, state per tick as in section 9, and exactly two questions: opponent_recovering (noul) and action (choice: advance, retreat, attack, block, bait). Reuse the wording in ~/projects/jev_latency.py for the question instructions and choice criteria, dropping anti_air and the score question. Use one persistent keep-alive HTTPS connection per fighter (http.client, as in jev_latency.py). Parse per the confirmed wire shape in ~/projects/jev_sample_response.json: choice has choice, confidence, probabilities dict; noul has noul only, no confidence; usage has input_tokens and output_tokens. Return a typed Decision (intent, probabilities, noul value, usage, round-trip ms). Tests in bridge/tests/ run offline against a copy of jev_sample_response.json. One live smoke call at the end. The API key is read from TYPESAFE_API_KEY at call time only; it must never be printed, logged, or written to any file, and must not appear in the test fixtures or the repo.
acceptance_criteria: 1) python3 -m unittest (or pytest) output shows the offline parser tests passing against the saved sample response. 2) One live call's parsed Decision is printed (intent, probabilities, usage, round-trip ms) with no key visible anywhere in the output. 3) grep -r TYPESAFE_API_KEY over the repo shows only os.environ reads.

title: Update start-app and stop-app skills for Stage 2: bridge plus MAME
description: The skills in .claude/skills/start-app and .claude/skills/stop-app currently describe Stage 1 (MAME plus a Lua script). Once the bridge exists, rewrite them so start-app launches the bridge from the project folder and MAME (with the main Lua script and the flags the bridge expects) from ~/mame, records both PIDs with labels in /tmp/sam2/pids, and states that it assumes Stage 2. stop-app must stop both. The skill must never describe a stage that no longer exists. Keep the PID guard, the refusal to start over a live PID, and the no-pkill rule.
acceptance_criteria: 1) .claude/skills/start-app/SKILL.md says it assumes Stage 2 and no longer presents Stage 1 as current. 2) Running /start-app then cat /tmp/sam2/pids shows two lines, mame and bridge, both alive per kill -0. 3) Running /stop-app reports both stopped and /tmp/sam2/pids is gone.

title: Python bridge skeleton with a dummy decision-maker for both fighters
description: Create bridge/ (Python 3, stdlib where possible; list any pip dependency in bridge/requirements.txt). Loop: watch /tmp/sam2/state.json (by mtime or seq), keep a rolling history of each fighter's current action to derive "opponent's last three actions", and at 3 Hz per fighter ask a DecisionMaker interface for an intent (advance / retreat / attack / block / bait). Ship a DummyDecisionMaker that cycles through intents on a fixed schedule. The bridge writes intent only to action.json via tmp+rename (decision on 21 Sep 2026: the executor lives in Lua; the bridge never chooses buttons). Log every decision with timestamp, fighter and intent to /tmp/sam2/bridge.log. Never block on file IO longer than one frame; note the measured loop time.
acceptance_criteria: 1) With the bridge and lua/start_match.lua running, I confirm on screen both characters act (walk, attack, block) with no human input for at least 30 seconds. 2) /tmp/sam2/bridge.log shows decisions for p1 and p2 at about 3 Hz each with their intents. 3) Notes state the measured bridge loop time. 4) grep over bridge/ shows no button names such as "P1 A"; only intents are written.

title: Lua reads intents from /tmp/sam2/action.json and applies a minimal expansion
description: Add the action reader to the main Lua script. Decision on 21 Sep 2026: the bridge sends intent only; all button expansion happens in Lua. Each frame, if /tmp/sam2/action.json is newer than the last one consumed (compare a seq number inside the file), parse it and apply it. Define the file format now and record it in notes and in docs/protocol.md: {"seq": n, "p1": {"intent": "advance|retreat|attack|block|bait"}, "p2": {...}}, optionally with a "source" field. For this task a minimal expansion is enough: advance holds toward the opponent, retreat holds away, block holds away, attack presses one attack button, bait presses an attack button then holds away, each for a fixed number of frames; the proper executor comes in Epic 7. Direction may be hard-coded (P1 left, P2 right) for now. Writers must write action.tmp then rename (PRD section 8). Test by hand: write an action.json from the shell while a match is running and watch the character respond.
acceptance_criteria: 1) docs/protocol.md describes action.json carrying intent per fighter, with a worked example. 2) I confirm on screen that hand-writing an action.json (via tmp+rename) with each of the five intents makes the named character do the minimal expansion during a live match. 3) A Lua log shows the seq numbers consumed.

title: Write /tmp/sam2/state.json every frame from the memory map and verify all fields live
description: Owns PRD section 12 item: "Memory addresses for health, position, move state". Add a state writer to the main Lua script: every frame, read every field in lua/memmap.lua and lua/moveids.lua and write PRD section 9 state (timer; per fighter: character name, position, health, rage, current action, airborne, crouching; gap between fighters) to /tmp/sam2/state.tmp then rename to state.json. The "opponent's last three actions" field is derived by the bridge, not here. Verify by recording 30 seconds of state.json samples (a Python watcher that appends each new file to /tmp/sam2/state_log.jsonl) during a live match while I watch.
acceptance_criteria: 1) /tmp/sam2/state.json contains every section 9 field for both fighters with the character names Earthquake and Nakoruru. 2) /tmp/sam2/state_log.jsonl from a 30-second live match shows health, position and current action all changing in step with events I confirm on screen. 3) Notes state the section 12 verification result for health, position and move state.

title: Find move-state IDs and decode 'in recovery' for Earthquake and Nakoruru
description: Owns PRD section 12 item: "Move IDs for Earthquake and Nakoruru". Using the harness: find the per-player current action / move-state byte(s). Drive each character through idle, walk, crouch, jump, block, each of the four attack buttons A, B, C, D (using the observed names from the A/B/C/D task, not assumed ones), and one whiffed heavy normal, using the Lua input helpers, and record the ID seen for each in lua/moveids.lua as two tables (earthquake, nakoruru). For each character identify which IDs mean "in recovery after an attack" and how the end of recovery is visible (ID changes back, or a frame counter). Log to /tmp/sam2/mem_moves.txt.
acceptance_criteria: 1) lua/moveids.lua contains an ID table per character covering at least idle, walk, crouch, jump, block, the four button attacks, and the recovery IDs. 2) /tmp/sam2/mem_moves.txt shows the ID changing at moments I confirm on screen for at least three of those moves per character. 3) Notes state the section 12 verification result and how recovery end is detected.

title: Find round timer, rage (POW) and airborne/crouching indicators for both players
description: Using the harness: find the round timer (decreases once a second, matches the on-screen number), the rage/POW gauge for each player (rises when hit), and a way to tell airborne and crouching for each player (either flags or derived from Y and a state byte). Log all values every frame to /tmp/sam2/mem_timer_rage.txt while I watch. Add to lua/memmap.lua.
acceptance_criteria: 1) lua/memmap.lua names timer, p1_rage, p2_rage and the airborne/crouching source for each player. 2) /tmp/sam2/mem_timer_rage.txt shows the timer value matching the on-screen number at two moments I confirm, and rage rising after a hit I confirm. 3) Notes say how airborne and crouching are derived.

title: Find health and X/Y position addresses for P1 and P2
description: Using the harness inside a live match: find P1 and P2 health (decreases when hit, resets each round), and P1 and P2 X and Y positions (X changes while walking, Y changes when jumping). Confirm by logging the candidate values every frame to /tmp/sam2/mem_health_pos.txt while I watch the match. Record addresses, widths, ranges (e.g. max health value) and whether the same addresses hold for both characters, in lua/memmap.lua as named constants and in notes. PRD section 8 infers these sit in player-slot memory shared by both characters; note whether that held.
acceptance_criteria: 1) lua/memmap.lua names addresses for p1_health, p2_health, p1_x, p1_y, p2_x, p2_y. 2) /tmp/sam2/mem_health_pos.txt shows health falling at the moments I confirm on screen a hit landed, and X moving while I confirm a walk. 3) Notes give the observed max health value and value ranges for X and Y.

title: Lua RAM diff-search harness over Neo Geo work RAM
description: Write lua/ramsearch.lua: snapshot a configurable range of maincpu program space (start at 0x100000, size 64 KiB, per probe.txt) into a Lua table, and on a key or timer diff it against the previous snapshot with filters: unchanged / changed / increased / decreased / equal to a value. Print candidate addresses with old and new values to /tmp/sam2/ramsearch.txt. Note whether 8-bit or 16-bit reads are used. It must run alongside lua/start_match.lua so searches happen inside a live Earthquake vs Nakoruru match.
acceptance_criteria: 1) /tmp/sam2/ramsearch.txt shows at least one snapshot-diff run with candidate addresses, old and new values, taken during a live match. 2) lua/ramsearch.lua is committed and its filter modes are listed in notes.

title: Lua starts an Earthquake vs Nakoruru match from cold boot with no human input
description: Combine coin/start and the select map into lua/start_match.lua: from MAME boot, insert coins, start both players, select Earthquake for P1 and Nakoruru for P2, confirm, and let round 1 begin. Log every input with frame numbers to /tmp/sam2/start_match.txt. Make the frame-count timing tolerant enough that three consecutive cold runs via /run-lua all reach the fight. This script becomes the Start sequence used by the bridge and the Tauri app (PRD section 6).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Three consecutive /run-lua runs of lua/start_match.lua from cold boot each reach round 1 with Earthquake on the left and Nakoruru on the right; I confirm each on screen. 2) /tmp/sam2/start_match.txt from the last run lists the full input sequence. 3) lua/start_match.lua is committed.

title: Map the character-select cursor path to Earthquake (P1) and Nakoruru (P2)
description: Determine, by driving the select screen from Lua with the Epic 1 helpers, the exact stick/button sequence (with frame counts between inputs) that moves the P1 cursor from its default position to Earthquake and the P2 cursor to Nakoruru, and what confirms each. Also determine how P2 joins: whether "2 Players Start" (port :edge:joy:START) or a second coin plus P2 start is needed. Write the findings to lua/select_map.lua as data (a table of steps) and to notes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) lua/select_map.lua contains the step tables for P1 to Earthquake and P2 to Nakoruru with frame gaps. 2) I confirm on screen that, when the tables are played back, the P1 cursor ends on Earthquake and the P2 cursor ends on Nakoruru. 3) Notes state how P2 joined.

title: Lua holds P1 Right during a fight and the character walks right
description: Owns PRD section 12 item: "set_value() moves a character in this game". Extend the Epic 1 script into lua/walk_right.lua: after coin and start, press P1 A (port :edge:joy:JOY1 field "P1 A") to accept the default character, wait a fixed number of frames for the round to begin, then hold field "P1 Right" for ~120 frames and release. Log the frame ranges to /tmp/sam2/walk_right.txt. Timing may be done with frame counts only; no memory reads yet. Record in notes whether set_value() on a digital field needs 1/0 or the field mask, and whether the value persists between frames or must be reasserted every frame.
acceptance_criteria: 1) I confirm on screen that the P1 character walks to the right for roughly two seconds during round 1 with no keyboard input. 2) /tmp/sam2/walk_right.txt shows the frame range in which P1 Right was held. 3) Notes state the verification result for the section 12 item and the set_value() value semantics found.

title: Lua inserts a coin and presses 1 Player Start from an autoboot script
description: Write lua/coin_start.lua in this repo. Using the exact port/field names in /tmp/sam2/probe.txt (port :AUDIO_COIN field "Coin 1"; port :edge:joy:START field "1 Player Start"), build a small helper that looks up a field by port tag and name and holds it for N frames via field:set_value(), driven from emu.add_machine_frame_notifier. After the autoboot delay: press Coin 1 for a few frames, release, wait, press 1 Player Start, release. Log each press with the frame number to /tmp/sam2/coin_start.txt. Run with /run-lua. This is the first use of set_value(); if it does not register, record what was tried in notes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) /tmp/sam2/coin_start.txt exists and lists Coin 1 and 1 Player Start presses with frame numbers. 2) I confirm on screen that the game left attract mode and reached the character select screen with no keyboard input from me. 3) lua/coin_start.lua is committed.
notes: Run 1 and run 2 via /run-lua lua/coin_start.lua 3. Log /tmp/sam2/coin_start.txt: both fields found (:AUDIO_COIN 'Coin 1' mask 0x1, :edge:joy:START '1 Player Start' mask 0x1); Coin 1 set at frame 300 / cleared 308; 1 Player Start set at 420 / cleared 428; no Lua errors in /tmp/sam2/mame.log. Observed by Zohaib, no keyboard input: PUSH START appeared over the attract demo fight (coin accepted), then the character portrait grid appeared (Start accepted), then the select timer expired and auto-picked a fighter; run 1 ended in a match with P1 standing idle until it lost. Findings for later tasks: (1) set_value(1)/clear_value() works on digital fields from a frame notifier; (2) Start is accepted while the attract demo is running, ~2 s after the coin at these frame counts; (3) the select screen auto-selects on timeout, so lua must move the cursor and confirm before then; (4) a started match with no input leaves P1 idle, a useful baseline for the walk test.

title: Epic 7: Executor move tables and reflex layer
description: PRD section 13 step 7. Record what A, B, C, D do per character, turn Jev intent into button presses over frames in Lua with per-character tables of movement and normals only, add the every-frame block-only reflex layer, and run a full Jev vs Jev match with no human input. Special moves and anti-air are v2 (PRD section 4).

title: Epic 6: Swap in Jev
description: PRD section 13 step 6. Replace the dummy with Jev (POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone) per the PRD section 9 contract: 3 Hz per fighter, parallel calls, newest wins, stale replies dropped, telemetry accounting, and the pause/reset/stop discard rule from section 6.

title: Epic 4: Find the memory addresses
description: PRD section 13 step 4. Locate in maincpu program space (probe.txt: Neo Geo work RAM at 0x100000) everything the Jev state per tick needs (PRD section 9): timer, and per fighter health, position, rage, current action / move state, airborne, crouching. Ends with a verified /tmp/sam2/state.json written every frame.

title: Epic 5: Bridge with a dummy decision-maker
description: PRD section 13 step 5. Python bridge exchanging /tmp/sam2/state.json and /tmp/sam2/action.json with the Lua script using write-tmp-then-rename, with a scripted dummy decision-maker in place of Jev. Includes the frame relay over WebSocket and the emulation-speed check from PRD section 12.

title: Epic 2: Lua selects Earthquake and Nakoruru and starts the match
description: PRD section 13 step 2. From a cold boot, Lua alone brings the game to round 1 of Earthquake (P1) vs Nakoruru (P2), and can take and reload a save state at match start for Reset (PRD section 6).

title: Epic 1: Make a character move from Lua
description: PRD section 13 step 1. Prove that a Lua autoboot script can drive the game: insert coins, start, reach a fight, and move a character with field:set_value(). Field names come from /tmp/sam2/probe.txt.

title: v2: Anti-air in the reflex layer
description: Deferred from v1 by decision on 21 Sep 2026: the v1 reflex layer is block only (PRD section 8 item 7). When v2 starts: add a rule that fires when the opponent is airborne and descending toward this fighter within reach, using an anti-air move chosen per character (depends on the v2 special-move task or an observed normal), tagged source reflex in presses.log.
acceptance_criteria: 1) I confirm on screen that a jump-in by one character is answered by the other with the chosen anti-air, at least twice per character. 2) /tmp/sam2/presses.log shows those presses with source reflex within a few frames of the opponent becoming airborne. 3) Notes name the anti-air move per character and the thresholds used.

title: v2: Special-move tables for Earthquake and Nakoruru, each move verified by an executor test
description: Deferred from v1 by decision on 21 Sep 2026: special moves are out of scope for v1 (PRD section 4). When v2 starts: agree the list of moves per character and which intent triggers them, encode each as a stick-and-button sequence with frame timings in lua/moves_earthquake.lua and lua/moves_nakoruru.lua, and add an executor test mode that fires each move by name from a test action.json.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Notes list the agreed moves per character and their triggering intent. 2) I confirm on screen each listed move comes out when fired by name via the executor test mode, for the right character. 3) Notes state per move whether it fires reliably.

title: Epic v2: Deferred from v1 (PRD section 4)
description: Work the PRD defers to v2. Nothing here starts before the v1 final acceptance run closes; each task is blocked by it. PRD section 4 "Deferred to v2" is the list of record.

title: Final acceptance run against PRD section 10
description: Using the built .app, run one complete session: Start, a full match to a winner, Pause and Resume once, Reset once, a second full match, Stop. Record emulation speed and view fps every second from the telemetry to /tmp/sam2/acceptance.log. Check each section 10 criterion and write the result per criterion in notes. This task does not fix anything; failures become new tasks.
acceptance_criteria: 1) /tmp/sam2/acceptance.log shows emulation speed at 100 percent and view fps at about 30 for the whole run, or notes state exactly where it dipped. 2) Notes list each section 10 criterion with pass or fail and the evidence. 3) I confirm on screen the run happened as described.

title: Pause, Resume, Reset and Stop buttons wired to the bridge with no stale presses after Reset
description: Connect the four controls to the bridge control channel (Epic 6 task). Pause toggles to Resume. Reset reloads the match-start save state, clears the panel and telemetry, and returns to round 1 with full health. Stop shuts down MAME and the bridge and keeps final totals on the panel. Verify the PRD section 6 rule end to end from the UI: press Reset repeatedly during a busy stretch and check that no press whose call was issued before the reset was applied afterwards.
acceptance_criteria: 1) I confirm on screen Pause freezes the game including the round timer, and Resume continues it. 2) I confirm Reset returns to round 1 with full health and a cleared panel. 3) /tmp/sam2/presses.log and bridge.log from a run with five Resets show zero presses applied from pre-reset calls; notes quote the check.

title: Telemetry panel part 2: Buttons, Timing and Usage sections
description: Per PRD section 7: Buttons held right now, total presses, and per-source counts (Jev / reflex). Timing: response time last and p50, decision time labelled on screen as estimated, calls made, stale responses discarded. Usage: input and output tokens running totals, cost running total. Totals must persist on screen after Stop (PRD section 6) and clear on Reset.
acceptance_criteria: 1) I confirm on screen all listed figures updating during a live match, with the word estimated visible next to decision time. 2) After Stop the totals remain; after Reset they read zero; I confirm both. 3) Notes pair the on-screen calls and stale figures with the bridge.log counts for the same run.

title: Telemetry panel part 1: match bar and Decision section for both fighters
description: Per PRD section 7: P1 and P2 side by side headed Earthquake and Nakoruru. Match bar: round timer, both health bars, emulation speed, view fps. Decision: current action and how long ago it was decided (live-updating), a probability bar for every action option, and a bar for the opponent_recovering yes/no question. All values come from the bridge telemetry object; nothing is computed from placeholders.
acceptance_criteria: 1) I confirm on screen every listed element for both fighters updating during a live match. 2) For one moment, notes pair a panel value (e.g. P1 action probabilities) with the matching bridge.log line.

title: Frame view: WebSocket JPEG frames drawn on a canvas at 30 fps
description: In the React UI, connect to the bridge WebSocket, decode each JPEG and draw it on a canvas scaled to the game view area with correct aspect ratio. Measure and display view fps in the match bar. Drop frames rather than queue them if the UI falls behind.
acceptance_criteria: 1) I confirm on screen the game playing inside the app window. 2) The view fps readout holds about 30 for a 60-second stretch; notes quote what I saw. 3) Notes state how frame dropping is done.

title: Start button reaches a live match end to end; controls enable only once it is running
description: Wire Start: app spawns bridge, bridge launches MAME with the Start sequence from Epic 2, and the bridge reports match-running over the WebSocket when round 1 begins. The app enables Pause, Reset and Stop only on that signal and disables Start. Show a status line with the current phase (booting, selecting, running, paused, stopped).
acceptance_criteria: 1) I confirm on screen that one press of Start ends in a live Earthquake vs Nakoruru match with the status line reading running. 2) I confirm Pause, Reset and Stop were disabled before that and enabled after. 3) Notes give the time from Start press to match running.

title: Update start-app and stop-app skills for Stage 3: the Tauri app
description: Rewrite .claude/skills/start-app and .claude/skills/stop-app for Stage 3: start-app launches the Tauri dev build (or the built .app; say which) and records its PID; the app owns bridge and MAME, so stop-app stops the app PID and then checks that bridge and MAME are gone too, reporting any orphan PIDs it finds in /tmp/sam2/pids without killing by name. The skill must state it assumes Stage 3 and must not describe Stage 2 as current.
acceptance_criteria: 1) .claude/skills/start-app/SKILL.md says it assumes Stage 3. 2) Running /start-app records the app PID in /tmp/sam2/pids and reports it alive. 3) Running /stop-app reports the app stopped and confirms no bridge or mame process remains.

title: Bridge runs as a Tauri sidecar; app launches bridge, bridge launches MAME; Stop shuts both down
description: Package the Python bridge as a Tauri sidecar (record how: bundled interpreter, PyInstaller, or a script sidecar, and why). On Start the app spawns the bridge; the bridge spawns MAME from ~/mame (cwd must be ~/mame because the rompath is relative) with -video none -sound none and the main Lua script, and inherits TYPESAFE_API_KEY from the environment without the app ever reading or logging it. On Stop the app sends stop to the bridge and confirms both processes exit; if the bridge does not exit within a timeout the app terminates it by PID, never by name.
acceptance_criteria: 1) After pressing Start, ps output shows the bridge and a mame process whose cwd is ~/mame. 2) After pressing Stop, the same ps shows neither. 3) grep over app/ shows no reference to TYPESAFE_API_KEY.

title: Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript app scaffold builds and opens a window on macOS
description: Create app/ with Tauri 2, React and TypeScript (record the exact create-tauri-app template and versions in notes). The window shows a placeholder layout: a game view area on top and a panel area below with Start, Pause, Reset, Stop buttons, Pause/Reset/Stop disabled. No process launching yet. Document the dev and build commands in app/README.md.
acceptance_criteria: 1) The dev command from app/README.md opens a native window titled for this project on this Mac; I confirm on screen. 2) The release build command completes and produces an .app bundle; notes give its path. 3) The three secondary buttons render disabled.

title: Reflex layer in Lua: block incoming attacks every frame, overriding Jev intent (v1: block only)
description: Decision on 21 Sep 2026: the v1 reflex layer is block only; anti-air is a v2 task. One plain rule run every frame in the Lua script using the memory map (PRD section 8 item 7): if the opponent is in an attack move ID and within reach, hold block (away; crouching if the attack is low, if that can be read from the move ID) until the attack ID ends, then return control to the current Jev intent. Reflex presses take precedence over the Jev intent and are tagged source reflex in presses.log. Thresholds (reach in pixels per attack ID, if needed) are recorded as constants with the observed values that led to them.
acceptance_criteria: 1) I confirm on screen that a slash at range by one character is blocked by the other at least three times, for both characters as defender. 2) /tmp/sam2/presses.log shows those presses with source reflex within a few frames of the opponent's move ID changing to an attack. 3) Notes list the threshold constants and how they were chosen.

title: Bridge control channel: pause, resume, reset, stop, with in-flight Jev calls discarded
description: Add a control channel to the bridge (same WebSocket, or a local command file; name the choice) with commands pause, resume, reset, stop. Decision on 21 Sep 2026: pause must be a real emulator pause through MAME's Lua API, and the bridge stops issuing Jev calls; withholding input is not acceptable because the round timer would keep running. First step of this task: read the MAME 0.289 Lua reference and confirm a pause/unpause call exists (record the exact call and doc location in notes); if none exists, stop and report, do not substitute. pause: Lua calls the pause API on a flag from the bridge, bridge stops calls. resume: unpause, restart calls. reset: Lua loads the match-start save state (Epic 2 task), bridge clears telemetry and restarts calls. stop: Lua exits MAME, bridge shuts down. Rule from PRD section 6: any call in flight when pause, reset or stop arrives is discarded on return (it must never press buttons) but still counted in calls, tokens and cost. Prove it with a scripted test that issues reset while calls are in flight and checks the log.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Notes name the MAME Lua pause API used and where the docs describe it. 2) I confirm on screen that during pause the round timer and the fighters are frozen, and that resume continues them; /tmp/sam2/bridge.log shows no calls issued while paused. 3) A test script output shows: after reset, zero presses were applied from calls issued before the reset, and those calls are still counted in calls and tokens. 4) I confirm on screen that reset returns to the start of round 1 with full health. 5) Notes record the control channel design.

title: Telemetry accounting: response time, estimated decision time, calls, stale, tokens, cost
description: In the bridge, maintain per fighter (PRD section 7): current action and when it was decided; probabilities for every action option; the noul value for opponent_recovering; response time last and p50 over the match; decision time estimated as round trip minus a network baseline measured at bridge start (TCP connect RTT as in jev_latency.py), labelled "estimated"; calls made; stale responses discarded; input and output token totals; running cost. Cost rule, confirmed by Typesafe AI on 21 Sep 2026: input tokens at 0.042 USD per million, output tokens at zero. Include all of it in the WebSocket telemetry object and show it as raw JSON in tools/view.html. Also include match-bar data: timer, both healths, emulation speed, and buttons currently held plus total presses per fighter with source jev or reflex.
acceptance_criteria: 1) tools/view.html shows every section 7 figure for both fighters updating during a live match; I confirm on screen. 2) Notes show one telemetry JSON sample with all fields present and non-zero calls. 3) The sum of calls equals applied plus stale in /tmp/sam2/bridge.log for the same run. 4) Notes show one cost figure recomputed by hand as input_tokens x 0.042 / 1e6, matching the telemetry value.

title: Measure emulation speed with frame writer and state/action exchange running together
description: Owns PRD section 12 item: "Frame file plus Jev files don't slow the game". Run the full Stage 2 stack: main Lua script with frame writer (every second frame) and state.json writer (every frame) and action reader, plus the bridge with the dummy decision-maker and the WebSocket relay with tools/view.html connected. Run a 60-second match under -video none and log emulation speed once a second to /tmp/sam2/speed_full.txt (same mechanism as the frame-writer task). Repeat with the frame writer disabled to get a comparison. Report both series in notes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) /tmp/sam2/speed_full.txt covers 60 seconds with everything running; notes quote min and median speed. 2) Notes quote the same figures with the frame writer off. 3) Notes state the section 12 verification result: whether speed stayed at 100 percent, and if not, by how much it dropped.

title: Bridge relays frames as JPEG over a WebSocket with telemetry, shown in a test page
description: In the bridge: watch /tmp/sam2/frame.meta, read frame.raw, convert using the pixel format recorded in the frame-grab task, JPEG-encode (name the library used and add it to requirements.txt), and push each frame plus a telemetry JSON object (whatever the dummy bridge knows: timer, health, current intents, decision timestamps) over a local WebSocket server. Add tools/view.html: a single static page that connects, draws frames on a canvas, and shows a measured frames-per-second counter and the raw telemetry JSON. Target 30 fps.
acceptance_criteria: 1) tools/view.html opened in a browser shows the live game and an fps counter reading about 30; I confirm on screen. 2) The telemetry JSON on the page changes as the match progresses. 3) Notes record the WebSocket port and the JPEG library and quality used.

title: Write every second frame to /tmp/sam2/frame.raw continuously
description: Extend the frame grab into the main Lua script: on every second frame (30 per second at 60 fps), call video:pixels() and write frame.tmp then rename to frame.raw. Add a frame counter and a timestamp to a small sidecar /tmp/sam2/frame.meta written the same way so a reader can tell frames apart. Log MAME's reported emulation speed (find the Lua property for speed percent in the docs, or read the OSD) once a second to /tmp/sam2/speed.txt while running for 60 seconds, windowed and under -video none.
acceptance_criteria: 1) /tmp/sam2/frame.meta advances by about 30 per second over a 10-second sample (two stat readings, quoted). 2) /tmp/sam2/speed.txt from a 60-second -video none run is present; notes quote the min and typical speed values. 3) A frame.png converted from a mid-run frame.raw shows the game.

title: Grab one frame with video:pixels() under -video none
description: Owns PRD section 12 item: "video:pixels() works with -video none". Run lua/grab_frame.lua again with MAME started as: mame samsho2 -video none -sound none -autoboot_script ... from ~/mame. Convert and view the result. If the frame is black, empty, or the call errors, record exactly what happened in notes and do not close; that result changes decision D2 and needs my call.
acceptance_criteria: 1) /tmp/sam2/frame.png produced from a -video none run shows game graphics (not black); I confirm on screen. 2) Notes contain the exact MAME command line used and the section 12 verification result (works / does not work).

title: Grab one frame with video:pixels() in windowed MAME and view it as a PNG
description: Write lua/grab_frame.lua: after the autoboot delay, call video:pixels() on the :screen device (find the correct object path in the MAME 0.289 Lua reference; do not assume), write the raw bytes to /tmp/sam2/frame.tmp then os.rename to /tmp/sam2/frame.raw. Record in notes the pixel format, byte order, width and height, and the byte count. Write a tiny stdlib-only Python converter tools/raw2png.py (or use Pillow if already installed; say which) to turn frame.raw into frame.png, and open it.
acceptance_criteria: 1) /tmp/sam2/frame.raw exists with the byte count matching width*height*bytes-per-pixel recorded in notes. 2) /tmp/sam2/frame.png opens and shows a recognisable Samurai Shodown II screen; I confirm on screen. 3) Notes record pixel format, dimensions and the exact Lua call used.

title: Save a state at match start from Lua and reload it to restart round 1
description: Owns PRD section 12 item: "Save and load state from Lua, for Reset". First read the MAME 0.289 Lua reference for save/load state (do not assume the API name; record in notes the exact call found, and whether it takes a slot name or a path). Then extend lua/start_match.lua: once round 1 begins, save a state; ~10 seconds later, load it. The game must jump back to the start of round 1 with full health for both. Record whether loading takes effect on the same frame or on the next.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Notes name the MAME Lua save/load API used and where the docs describe it. 2) I confirm on screen that the match rewinds to the start of round 1 with full health after the load call. 3) /tmp/sam2/start_match.txt logs the frame numbers of the save and load calls. 4) Notes state the section 12 verification result.

title: Epic 8: Tauri shell, controls, frame view, panel
description: PRD section 13 step 8. Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript app: Start/Pause/Reset/Stop per section 6, canvas frame view at 30 fps, telemetry panel per section 7, final acceptance against section 10.
